lines.trans: Look how neat every page is: date, room number, guest name, and weather.
Turn to May tenth, Suad—the Friday written on our postcard!
Here it is! "Heavy rain all night; water dripped onto the sunroom piano."
Read the next line: "Moved the piano to the dry corner; middle key swollen shut."
Oh! That rainy night broke the roof and jammed middle D at the same time!
Look at my aunt's note underneath: "Locked Room Nine until the roof is dry."
And she tucked her unfinished waltz inside the lid to wait for sunny weather!
Then summer guests filled the house, years passed, and the bookcase went up.
She never got to hear the second half of her Friday waltz.
Mazen, with your permission, may I write the missing sixteen bars for Wednesday?
You would finish my aunt's song for our reopening, Suad?!
In the very same key, with her opening melody leading us home.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for both casual 'yes / yeah' and 'oh! / ah!' upon noticing something.

examples.trans: Oh, the door opened! Thank you.
Yes, eight rooms and eight keys.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; the plural أغاني (aghaani) is the one you hear most.

examples.trans: This is an old song my grandmother loves.
We listen to songs in the car every morning.

meanings.note: Name of the month of May in the Levantine calendar.

examples.trans: My birthday is in May.
In May the weather gets nice in Amman.

meanings.note: Used constantly in the polite phrase عن إذنك ('excuse me / with your permission').

examples.trans: Excuse me, may I pass?
He asked permission before heading out.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.trans: What is your kind name?
My name is written here in the notebook.

meanings.note: Official opening day or evening of a café, exhibition, or hall.

examples.text: افتتاح الكافيه رح يكون بآخر الأسبوع.
examples.trans: The café opening will take place at the end of the week.

examples.text: عزمنا كل الجيران على ليلة الافتتاح.
examples.trans: We invited all the neighbours to opening night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: The holy day in Islam and the weekend in Jordan.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Levantine passive Form VII of حط ('to put/place').

examples.trans: The new tables were placed under the arch.
The green ledger was put away in the attic chest.

meanings.note: Opening section of a song, book, or week.

examples.trans: The opening of the song is gentle and lifts the heart.

examples.text: من بداية الربيع، الساحة بتتعبى ورد.
examples.trans: From the start of spring, the courtyard fills with blossoms.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'then, next, afterwards' (وبعدين 'and then').

examples.trans: Lift the handle first, and then push.
Have some tea and then we will talk.

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Means both a calendar 'date' (تاريخ البطاقة 'the date on the card') and 'history'.

examples.trans: Write today's date at the top of the page.

examples.text: هاد البيت القديم إله تاريخ حلو بعمان.
examples.trans: This old house has a lovely history in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian expression to express surprise or ask for confirmation, like 'really?' or 'seriously!'.

examples.trans: My grandfather's workshop was on this street.
Did you really finish all the work?

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبي, بيخبي).

examples.trans: Why did you save it away for me all these years?
She tucked the recipe away in the kitchen notebook.

meanings.note: Transitive, with a doubled middle r (kharrab): someone breaks something. Written the same as خرب; the past خربت is 'I broke' (kharrabt) or 'it broke down' (khirbat) depending on context.

examples.trans: The boy broke the toy on the first day.
Be careful not to break the lock!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خزاين.

examples.trans: The clean towels are in the linen closet.
We locked the suitcase inside the closet.

meanings.note: Form II causative of رجع ('come back').

examples.trans: I put the keys back in the desk drawer.

examples.text: هاد اللحن القديم بيرجعنا لأيام زمان.
examples.trans: This old melody takes us back to the old days.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Solfege name standard in Arabic music education for the note D (ري الوسطى 'middle D').

examples.text: نغمة ري الوسطى هي المفتاح اللي كان ساكت.
examples.trans: Middle D is the exact key that was silent.

examples.text: الأغنية بتنزل بهدوء على نغمة ري بالأخير.
examples.trans: The song settles gently onto D near the end.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 16; before a counted singular noun it may appear as سطاش or سطاعشر.

examples.text: مدام سعاد رح تكتب السطاش مازورة الناقصة.
examples.trans: Madam Suad is going to write the sixteen missing bars.

examples.text: صفينا سطاش فنجان أبيض على الرف.
examples.trans: We lined up sixteen white cups on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطوح.

examples.trans: We heard the sound of rain on the roof.
From the rooftop we see the hills of Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطور.

examples.trans: Read me the top line of the letter.
He wrote two short lines on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite no -a ending.

examples.trans: The warm sun came out after the rain.
Read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Describes bright, rain-free sky after clouds or storms.

examples.text: بعد ليلة المطر، فاق الصبح على صحو وشمس.
examples.trans: After the rainy night, morning broke to clear skies and sunshine.

examples.text: عم نستنى يوم صحو عشان ندهن الكراسي برا.
examples.trans: We're waiting for a clear dry day to paint the chairs outside.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صفحات.

examples.trans: Read the second page of the letter.
The notebook fell open to the middle page.

meanings.note: The season of summer.

examples.trans: Evenings in Amman are pleasant in summer.
Our rent is paid until next summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: ضيفة). Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The weather in Amman is mild in spring.
I looked out the window to check the weather.

meanings.note: Can refer to physical length, height, or duration of time (e.g., all day).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: The standalone number ten.

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Form I intransitive verb ('iliq / byi'laq) meaning 'get stuck or jammed'; contrast transitive علّق ('hang up / jam').

examples.text: المفتاح القديم علق بالقفل من الصدا.
examples.trans: The old key got stuck in the lock from rust.
The sheet of paper got wedged behind the wooden rest.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعلق, بيعلق).

examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror?
We hung the lanterns in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Arabic distinguishes father's sister (عمة, feminine of عمّ) from mother's sister (خالة).

examples.text: عمتي كانت تعزف عالبيانو كل يوم جمعة.
examples.trans: My paternal aunt used to play the piano every Friday.

examples.text: هاد الدفتر الأخضر هدية من عمتي.
examples.trans: This green notebook is a gift from my aunt.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Standard collocation with rain: مطر غزير ('heavy downpour').

examples.text: نزل مطر غزير طول الليل وغسل الشجر.
examples.trans: Heavy rain fell all night and washed the trees clean.

examples.text: النشرة بتتوقع مطر غزير لبكرا الضهر.
examples.trans: The forecast predicts heavy rain until tomorrow noon.

meanings.note: Refers to a lid, cover, or sometimes a blanket.

examples.trans: Put the lid on the pot.
In winter I sleep under a heavy blanket.

meanings.note: Musical loanword (from French valse) for a triple-time piano or orchestral waltz.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد فالس هادي بغرفة القزاز.
examples.trans: Suad played a gentle waltz in the sunroom.

examples.text: عنوان الورقة القديمة هو فالس الساحة.
examples.trans: The title on the old sheet is Courtyard Waltz.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقفل, بيقفل).

examples.trans: We locked your suitcase safe in the storage closet.
I lock the iron gate at night.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Depending on vowels, it means 'he wrote' (katab) or plural 'books' (kutub).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; كرت بريد means 'postcard'. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Used intransitively (تكمل قبل الجمعة 'to be finished before Friday') alongside transitive كمّل ('to complete something').

examples.text: رح تكمل الغرفة أول ما نرتب الكراسي.
examples.trans: The room will be complete as soon as we arrange the chairs.

examples.text: الفرحة ما بتكمل إلا بوجود الجيران.
examples.trans: The celebration is only complete with the neighbours there.

meanings.note: Used to mark the limit of a time period, distance, or extent in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: We waited until you called us.
I stayed up until midnight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلحق, بيلحق).

examples.trans: Follow me quickly to the third floor!

examples.text: لحقنا دكان الخردوات أول ما فتح.
examples.trans: We caught the hardware shop right as it opened.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألحان.

examples.trans: She played old melodies on the piano.
This gentle tune is familiar to me.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليالي.

examples.trans: The guest arrived last night.
The neighbourhood is very quiet at night.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic conservatory/musicians' term (from Italian misura) for one bar of music.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد أول أربع مازورات من الفالس.
examples.trans: Suad played the first four bars of the waltz.

examples.text: اللحن بيوقف بنص المازورة الرابعة والعشرين.
examples.trans: The melody stops in the middle of the twenty-fourth bar.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمر, بيمر).

examples.trans: Pass right beside the green pharmacy.

examples.text: أنا مريت من جنب السبيل الحجري!
examples.trans: I just passed the stone fountain!

meanings.note: Used to describe a neat person, a well-organized room, or generally something of high quality (e.g. 'a nice car').

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting right away.
Neat pencil sketches.

meanings.note: Describes weather or a place receiving plenty of sunlight.

examples.trans: Please sit beside the sunny window.
The sunny attic room overlooks the courtyard.

meanings.note: Standard word for rain, commonly used across all registers of Arabic.

examples.trans: Please come inside out of the cold rain.
The trees are green and lovely after the rain.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: In Arabic music, names both a traditional melodic mode (maqam) and a Western musical key.

examples.text: سعاد كتبت التكملة على نفس المقام بالزبط.
examples.trans: Suad wrote the continuation in the exact same key.

examples.text: هاد اللحن مكتوب على مقام دافي وهادي.
examples.trans: This melody is written in a warm, gentle key.

meanings.note: Often used as a noun meaning 'letter' (mail) or 'destiny' in traditional contexts.

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

meanings.note: Used for remarks, annotations, or paying attention to details.

examples.trans: He wrote all the street notes in the notebook.
Thank you for that helpful observation.

meanings.note: Everyday verb meaning 'fill a house, jug, or basket'.

examples.text: ريحة الخبز السخن ملت الساحة كلها.
examples.trans: The scent of hot bread filled the entire courtyard.

examples.text: ضيوف الصيف ملوا كل غرف البيت.
examples.trans: Summer guests filled every room of the house.

meanings.note: Describes a rainy day, season or night (يوم ممطر 'a rainy day').

examples.trans: It was a cold, rainy day.
Winter this year is very rainy.

meanings.note: Used to ask for permission 'is it possible?' or to say 'perhaps'.

examples.trans: May I see the room first?
Could I see the tag in the sunlight?

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Can refer to objects lacking moisture or metaphorically to a rude or blunt person.

examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat.
The attic is dry and warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناقصة, plural: ناقصين).

examples.trans: Tell me what is missing in the room?

examples.text: الأغراض كاملة ما فيها شي ناقص.
examples.trans: Everything is complete with nothing missing.

meanings.note: Form I intransitive verb (nishif / byinshaf) meaning 'dry out'.

examples.text: لما تطلع الشمس، الحجار بتنشف بسرعة.
examples.trans: When the sun comes out, the stones dry quickly.

examples.text: استنينا ساعتين لحد ما ينشف الدهان.
examples.trans: We waited two hours until the paint dried.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نغمات.

examples.text: سمع كل نغمة من البيانو بهدوء.
examples.trans: He listened quietly to every note of the piano.
The chime of the bell is gentle, not harsh.

meanings.note: Describes wood swelling from dampness as well as blowing air.

examples.text: الخشب القديم نفخ شوي من رطوبة الشتا.
examples.trans: The old wood swelled slightly from the winter damp.
The pastry puffed up in the oven and turned golden.

meanings.note: Often used to mean 'the same' when followed by a noun, or as a reflexive.

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنقط, بينقط).

examples.text: آسف نقطت مي على أرضكم النظيفة.
examples.trans: Sorry I dripped water on your clean floor.
The pipe stopped dripping.

meanings.note: Vocalized lemma distinguishing the verb 'to move/relocate' from the noun نقل ('transport').

examples.trans: We moved the piano to the dry corner of the room.

examples.text: نور نقلت المواعيد من الدفتر للوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: Nour copied the dates from the notebook onto the whiteboard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian distal demonstrative ('that over there / that past...'); feminine هديك (hadiik), plural هدولاك.

examples.text: بتذكر هداك الربيع لما فتحنا النزل؟
examples.trans: Do you remember that spring when we opened the inn?

examples.text: حط الصندوق على هداك الرف العالي.
examples.trans: Put the box on that high shelf.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian presentative word ('here is! / look!') pointing to someone or something right now; takes suffixes (هيهم hayy-hum 'here they are!').

examples.text: هي تاكسي وقف عند الباب هلا!
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just stopped at the door!
Here they come down the stairs!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian adjective from وسط ('middle'); pairs naturally with المفتاح الوسطاني and ري الوسطى.

examples.text: المفتاح الوسطاني بالبيانو كان عالق من الرطوبة.
examples.trans: The middle key on the piano was stuck from dampness.

examples.text: الطاولة الوسطانية بالساحة بتاخد أحلى شمس.
examples.trans: The middle table in the courtyard catches the nicest sunshine.

meanings.note: General term for time or duration.

examples.trans: Old pipes take time to warm up.
You arrived right on time.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
